displayedInputs.question:
Three concentric circles centered at \(O\) have radii of \(1,\) \(2,\) and \(3.\) Points \(B\) and \(C\) lie on the largest circle. The region between the two smaller circles is shaded, as is the portion of the region between the two larger circles bounded by central angle \(BOC,\) as shown in the figure below. Suppose the shaded and unshaded regions are equal in area. What is the measure of \(\angle BOC\) in degrees?

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

Jordan owns \(15\) pairs of sneakers. Three fifths of the pairs are red and the rest are white. Two thirds of the pairs are high-top and the rest are low-top. The red high-top sneakers make up a fraction of the collection. What is the least possible value of this fraction?

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

Any three vertices of the cube \(PQRSTUVW,\) shown in the figure below, can be connected to form a triangle. (For example, vertices \(P,\) \(Q,\) and \(R\) can be connected to form isosceles \(\bigtriangleup PQR.\)) How many of these triangles are equilateral and contain \(P\) as a vertex?

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

A roll of tape is \(4\) inches in diameter and is wrapped around a ring that is \(2\) inches in diameter. A cross section of the tape is shown in the figure below. The tape is \(0.015\) inches thick. If the tape is completely unrolled, approximately how long would it be? Round your answer to the nearest \(100\) inches.

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

Rodrigo has a very large piece of graph paper. First he draws a line segment connecting point \((0, 4)\) to point \((2, 0)\) and colors the \(4\) cells whose interiors intersect the segment, as shown below. Next, Rodrigo draws a line segment connecting point \((2000, 3000)\) to point \((5000, 8000).\) Again he colors the cells whose interiors intersect the segment. How many cells will he color this time?

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

Jean made a piece of stained glass art in the shape of two mountains, as shown in the figure below. One mountain peak is \(8\) feet high and the other peak is \(12\) feet high. Each peak forms a \(90^\circ\) angle, and the straight sides of the mountains form \(45^\circ\) angles with the ground. The artwork has an area of \(183\) square feet. The sides of the mountains meet at an intersection point near the center of the artwork, \(h\) feet above the ground. What is the value of \(h?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

A small airplane has \(4\) rows of seats with \(3\) seats in each row. Eight passengers have boarded the plane and are distributed randomly among the seats. A married couple is next to board. What is the probability there will be \(2\) adjacent seats in the same row for the couple?

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

A semicircle has diameter \(AB\) and chord \(CD\) of length \(16\) parallel to \(AB.\) A smaller semicircle with diameter on \(AB\) and tangent to \(CD\) is cut from the larger semicircle, as shown below.

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

What is the area of the resulting figure, shown shaded?

mappings.rationale: Each distinct interior grid-line crossing starts a new cell. Count the union of horizontal and vertical crossings, subtracting coincident crossings at lattice vertices; the lattice-point count is a substep rather than the requested cell count.
mappings.answerReason: The coordinate changes are 3000 and 5000. There are 2999 interior vertical crossings and 4999 interior horizontal crossings. Since gcd(3000,5000)=1000, exactly 999 crossings coincide at lattice vertices. Including the initial cell gives 1+2999+4999−999=7000.

mappings.rationale: The 45° sides make horizontal runs equal to their corresponding vertical rises. Find the composite area either by completing both mountain triangles and subtracting their overlap, or by vertical triangle-and-trapezoid dissection, then take the positive height.
mappings.answerReason: A completed mountain of height H has base 2H and area H². The overlap is another such triangle of height h, so 8²+12²−h²=183. Therefore h²=25 and h=5 feet.

mappings.rationale: The four vacant seats form a uniformly chosen subset of the twelve seats. Classify vacancy counts by row, either counting the complement or favorable patterns directly; the two end seats of a row are not adjacent.
mappings.answerReason: There are C(12,4)=495 vacancy subsets. With no adjacent vacancies, row patterns 1+1+1+1, 2+1+1, and 2+2 contribute 3⁴=81, 4·C(3,2)·3²=108, and C(4,2)=6 subsets. Thus the probability is 1−195/495=20/33. Direct favorable counting also gives 36+48+216=300 subsets.

mappings.rationale: Subtract the two semicircle areas. Tangency makes the chord's height above AB equal to the smaller radius, while the perpendicular from the larger circle's center bisects the chord and supplies a right triangle.
mappings.answerReason: Let the larger and smaller radii be R and r. The distance from the larger center to CD is r, and half the chord is 8. Thus R²−r²=8²=64, so the shaded area is π(R²−r²)/2=32π.
